commands.name: fpga-batch
commands.help: the batched wire protocol design gate: conformance/tern_tc_batch_model.py --self-test (BatchCell reference model of specs/trinet/tern_tc_batch_ax7203.t27 — SETX/DOT6 frames, the RAM-read preimage rule, negative controls incl. RAM drift after SETX); exit 0 PASS

commands.name: fpga-batch-cosim
commands.help: conformance/tern_tc_batch_rtl_cosim.py: the rehearsal's recorded request stream replayed through formal/tern_tc_layer_rtl_tb.v under iverilog vs a fresh HuntingBatchCell (byte-for-byte; negative control = blind 24-byte framing). Pre-built red: FAILs on the current core at the first SETX tag (no SETX/DOT6 ops yet); PASS is the TERN_TC_BATCH_RTL_PLAN.md core edit's gate. The walk_answers precondition refuses non-adjudicable streams (out-of-range phantom frames: model drops, RTL will answer) loudly instead of reporting a mystery diff; needs iverilog+vvp

commands.name: fpga-batch-rehearsal
commands.help: the batched protocol's job stream: conformance/tern_tc_batch_runner.py --self-test (26 checks — whole passes pipelined through one window, mixed 19/24-byte answers shaped by issued nonces and settled by tag — natural y-nonce collisions hit ~1% of DOT6 frames and resolve without a false stop, loss recovery over RxLoss/TxLoss/the hunting parser, zero-plane skip, per-row recombination vs the int8 oracle, the honest/corrupt rehearsal pair); exit 0 PASS

commands.name: fpga-budget
commands.help: wire budget of a finished generation run: request and answer streams in bytes and seconds-alone, each share of the wall clock, in-run jobs/s against the link ceiling, request-bound or answer-bound verdict; REQ_LEN/RESP_LEN/BAUD come from the spec the log cites (the decode chain, stopped at the first spec pinning them), retransmit frames counted into the request stream and labelled approximate; refuses a live, short-verified, elapsed-less or constant-less log

commands.name: fpga-build
commands.help: build a node bitstream locally (openXC7, prjxray-db ab1fc60); never touches the board, only prints the flash command (conformance/NODE_TOOLCHAIN_RESTORE.md)

commands.name: fpga-claim
commands.help: loop iteration lock (exit 75 = held by another)

commands.name: fpga-cost
commands.help: LUT/FF/CARRY4/DSP/BRAM (B36+B18) under four synth_xilinx flag sets and the spread of the difference: a gap below the spread is the mapper, not the design; BRAM is how an inferred RAM is proven to have inferred (FF inflation means it did not)

commands.name: fpga-decode
commands.help: the board ids of a generation log as text; refuses unless every receipt verified, exit 0, board ids = CPU_INT_IDS, the model sha is the generation spec's and the tokenizer vocabulary equals the model's (the local results/step2 tokenizer is 32000, the model 8192: refused)

commands.name: fpga-derive
commands.help: rebuild the kept corpus from its chain (~/t27 at the pinned commit via git archive, the sibling's t27_bench.py + data.py with the held-copy patch, items/tokenizer from the keep blobs) and sha256-verify every MANIFEST.tsv row tagged keep:ft_t27_8k; 91/92 rows byte-identical, manifest.json checked on content, proven fire 29

commands.name: fpga-fire
commands.help: open the NEXT fire: lock row + fire-log stub built in memory, linted, written as ONE atomic edit (the fire-18 protocol made mechanical); refuses if a fire is IN-PROGRESS or the file does not lint; numbers above the archive max too; the DONE flip and full log entry stay hand-written

commands.name: fpga-firelog
commands.help: move fire-log entries whose fires lost their LOCKS rows to .claude/loop/firelog-archive.md (verbatim, never dropped; archive written first so a crash duplicates rather than loses); the linter counts a fire's entry in either home

commands.name: fpga-flash
commands.help: load a bitstream into SRAM (sudo openocd, the owner types the password); refuses without the owner's quoted yes, with openocd running, with an existing log or a foreign payload, or while a board run holds the UART lock (exit 75); records everything in board_runs/NAME.log; the key is wiped after a load

commands.name: fpga-genscore
commands.help: score t27_bench gen candidates for a behavioral criterion: literal >=N-line count AND degeneracy-filtered count (unique stripped lines < half the body = repetition loop, fire 35); the verdict rides the FILTERED count at --pass-frac of rows; in the tools self-test sweep

commands.name: fpga-hole
commands.help: UART hole size from nonce arithmetic (expected = 0x10000 + verified; every hex header must give the same number), not by eye

commands.name: fpga-hostnet
commands.help: before a LAN run: the route to IP is direct on a local interface (no gateway, no VPN tunnel), IP is in its subnet and not this Mac, no ARP entry yet; exit 0 ok, 2 stop; sends nothing

commands.name: fpga-ioclients
commands.help: who holds IOKit user clients on the CP2102N (pid, count, alive) and which driver is bound (AppleUSBSLCOM or a vendor one); every fpga-run header gets "# usb clients" and "# usb driver" lines

commands.name: fpga-jtag
commands.help: JTAG chain behind a Xilinx Platform Cable USB II (DLC10, 03fd): fxload only on --load (no sudo), xc3sprog -c xpc -j, each IDCODE named; no chain -> raw TDO shift classified (all ones = nothing drives TDO: VREF/ribbon/orientation; all zeros = TDO held low: cable). Never programs. Exit 0 chain, 1 none, 2 no cable

commands.name: fpga-keep
commands.help: keep a volatile /tmp tree durably: every file -> artifacts/model_inputs/blobs/<sha256> (gitignored) + a MANIFEST.tsv row (tracked), pins tag keep:TAG; after that tmpcheck watches the tree and --restore rebuilds it after a reboot (fire 28: the round-1 corpus had no builder, only /tmp and a stopped pod); in the tools self-test sweep

commands.name: fpga-keycheck
commands.help: how many times the key occurs in each file (prints counts, never the key); no FILE = every board_runs/ and rehearsal_runs/ log, also flags logs >= 1 MB

commands.name: fpga-loopcheck
commands.help: the standing per-fire sweep in one call: git status (informational), specs, keycheck, audit, one greppable verdict line; exit is the OR of the three real components

commands.name: fpga-loopstate
commands.help: lint .claude/loop-state.md (read-only): sections, UART lock paragraph, exactly one fresh IN-PROGRESS row, every table fire in the fire log (live file or the firelog archive); loopcheck runs it as its fifth component, so a broken coordination file fails the sweep instead of being inherited by the next cron fire

commands.name: fpga-pins
commands.help: the blast radius of editing FILE, before the edit: every spec pinning it by sha256 transitively (L1 direct, L2 pinners of pinners, ...) plus the params generators inside the radius — the exact set fpga-repin will then walk. Reports pin cycles (exit 1); read-only

commands.name: fpga-prcheck
commands.help: before a PR: bare #N refs, the Claude Code trailer, estimated stamps, and a fork behind with workflow changes the token cannot push; exit 0 ready, 2 not; posts nothing

commands.name: fpga-push
commands.help: fetch, rebase, key check of the outgoing patch, push with the gHashTag token (HANDOFF section 9), no force

commands.name: fpga-quiet
commands.help: wait until the 1-min load stays <= X per cpu for HOLD s; exit 0 quiet, 1 if WAIT passes first; starts nothing. Run it before a one-attempt board run

commands.name: fpga-rehearse
commands.help: COMMAND... — a no-board rehearsal twice at once into rehearsal_runs/NAME_{1,2}.log; refuses --port, /dev/, the key file, openocd; exit 0 only if both pass with the same events (wall-clock times masked). --compare LOG1 LOG2 compares two logs

commands.name: fpga-release
commands.help: loop iteration lock (exit 75 = held by another)

commands.name: fpga-repin
commands.help: propagate a sha256 change of FILE through the pin graph to a fixpoint: leaf pins, cross-spec pins, params regeneration, params pins. Never guesses: a missing pinned file is skipped with a note, an ambiguous *_SHA256 is refused, a generator PROBLEM stops the walk. Exit 0 = converged, 1 = changes made/pending, 2 = refused/PROBLEM

commands.name: fpga-restore
commands.help: the post-power-event chain in one command: probe the JTAG chain (no sudo; idcode 0x13636093 = the XC7A200T answers, all-ones = board power, no device = the FTDI half-enumeration wedge), then the fpga-flash load, then discover_port.py for the UART (status 0x04 after a fresh load is normal: no key yet), then the whole chain as one note on the task

commands.name: fpga-run
commands.help: COMMAND... — one board run into board_runs/NAME.log with the standard wrapper; never overwrites an existing log (one attempt, both runs on record)

commands.name: fpga-runlog
commands.help: one command for a run's progress: grammar-parsed status of a live (polls) or finished board_runs log; --self-test

commands.name: fpga-rxcap
commands.help: E3 RX capture at the RX flip-flops in the same SDF (conformance/e3_rx_capture_model.py; spec specs/trinet/e3_rx_capture_model_ax7203.t27; reads /tmp/e3txhold, pinned by sha, runs no tool): with no argument prints the one recorded run (conformance/model_runs/e3_rx_capture_model.log) if it exists, else runs it once (seconds); exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 NO VERDICT. PASS 00:21Z 2026-09-28: falling-edge hold 10900 ps on rxctl_n; RXC 2.4 ns behind its data through the BUFG, so rxd_p1 and an RX_ER nibble sample the new value over x -2.5..+0.5 ns (board ed should stay 0)

commands.name: fpga-rxer
commands.help: E3 RX_ER cases in simulation (conformance/eth_rxer_bench.py, about 4.5 min at nice 19): the pinned TB, model and RTL compiled unchanged plus formal/eth_rxer_inject.v as a second top that forces RX_CTL at one falling RXC edge; expectations fixed in NODE_ETHERNET_PLAN.md; exit 1 if any case disagrees. --gate also runs each case on the yosys netlist (the runner's gate_netlist) and requires every INJ/RXE/TXF/TB/UART| line of the gate log to equal the RTL log; each gate run took 28 to 30 min at nice 19 under load (15/15 at 22:35Z, 91b07fd86). Rerun after any E3 RTL change

commands.name: fpga-seeds
commands.help: Fmax as a distribution over nextpnr-xilinx seeds: CSV row per seed (LUT/FF/CARRY4, post-route Fmax, logic/routing ns) + min/median/max; warns when cell counts differ; --run keeps one log per seed, refuses overwrite, writes input sha256s + nextpnr version

commands.name: fpga-selftest
commands.help: off-board --self-test of every conformance/*.py a .t27 spec names (RUNNER or *_FILE); refuses a self_test that opens a port (exit 2 = fail/missing/refused)

commands.name: fpga-specs
commands.help: every conformance/*_from_spec.mjs --check: .t27 specs compile, test blocks pass, generated files have not drifted (exit 2 = drift)

commands.name: fpga-stamps
commands.help: the audit's stamp check alone: HH:MM stamps that postdate the commit that wrote them, over the claim docs, plus its calibration probe (stamp_probe steps the probe commit back across midnight so it stays inside the check's same-date scope at every instant — the fire-27 bug); in the tools self-test sweep

commands.name: fpga-status
commands.help: USB (UART behind a hub?), openocd, lock, what is loaded (from the latest flash log), latest runs (verdict or exit), git

commands.name: fpga-steps
commands.help: where a pre-registered board sequence stands (default plan NODE_ETHERNET_PLAN.md, e.g. KEY=E3; FILE is looked up here, then in conformance/; KEY is the start of the heading, e.g. "The board run" --plan UART_LOSS_HUBFREE.md): each tri fpga-run/-flash line against its board_runs log, commands that differ from the plan, out-of-order logs, the next step; prints only, runs nothing, judges nothing; exit 2 on a problem

commands.name: fpga-tmpcheck
commands.help: every file a .t27 spec pins by sha256 under /tmp (emptied at boot): ok / CHANGED / GONE and whether a kept copy exists in trinity-fpga/artifacts/model_inputs/blobs (gitignored; MANIFEST.tsv tracked). --archive keeps present files, --restore puts kept ones back where gone (never over a CHANGED file); fpga-audit flags lost and unkept inputs and --heal does both. Exit 0 all kept, 1 some unkept or unlocated, 2 a pin lost

commands.name: fpga-tools
commands.help: every board-tool's own --self-test in one call (runlog, budget, tmpcheck, decode, repin, pins, fire, firelog), one verdict line; loopcheck runs it as its fourth component, so each fire re-verifies the whole tool layer after any edit

commands.name: fpga-tristate
commands.help: pads whose output enable comes out inverted (OLOGIC pad pip or routed T1 input without ZINV_T1; exit 1); the archived nextpnr-xilinx drops that bit under router1

commands.name: fpga-txhold
commands.help: E3 TX hold and setup at the TX output buffers in nextpnr-xilinx's own SDF of the routed e3z (conformance/e3_tx_hold_model.py; spec specs/trinet/e3_tx_hold_model_ax7203.t27): with no argument prints the one recorded run (conformance/model_runs/e3_tx_hold_model.log) if it exists, else runs it once (about 2.5 min, needs /tmp/trinet-node-build/e3z); exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 NO VERDICT. PASS 23:23Z 2026-09-27: smallest hold 3445 ps on TXD1, bench 3000; the model has no clock skew. Another build or RTL needs its own spec

commands.name: fpga-usb
commands.help: CP2102N placement: DIRECT/HUB by the locationID rule, cross-checked by the hub-class walk of uart_loss_hubfree_ax7203.py --usb (exit 1 = HUB, 3 = the two rules disagree)

commands.name: fpga-watch-clients

Env: SC_OUT (default results/t27/selfcheck1), SC_ROUNDS (5), SC_ARMS (m0.8,w0.8,m0.7,w0.7 -- w = wide VALUE-core rule), SC_ITEMS (30), SC_STOP (pass|compile), SC_SEED=<int> (deterministic per-job sampling seeds; PAIRED A/Bs:   same seed base + same arms = identical streams, a pass delta is   causal; without it tc_fast is time-seeded and 30-item pass counts   are noise -- 2026-09-29 base30 3 vs repair30 0 on same code paths) SC_WORKERS (3), SC_REPAIR=1 (strip module-level lines + unterminated strings; keep ON), SC_EARLY=1 (abort repetition tail-locks mid-decode via engine "x", cascade_abort n=6/reps=3 -- gold-safe 0/466, catches 22/218 cascades; measured WEAK, A/B before trusting) SC_ITEMS_FILE=<jsonl> (default t27/items.jsonl): a different item set, e.g. results/t27/selftrain/items.jsonl (train-side yield; use SC_POOL=strict). NOTE the mask core is computed from that file too. SC_POOL=strict = every strict item (both mutants caught) of items.jsonl -- the honest full-bench number; NOTE --n-items still CUTS the pool after picking, so pass SC_ITEMS=500 with strict (the 2026-09-29 trap that silently ran 30 of 391), SC_KV_I8=1 (int8 KV cache: ~1.6x at 1.7K ctx, approximate -- pass numbers not comparable to f32-KV runs). SC_ANALYZE=1: free selector oracle over the committed v1/v2/v3 mask artifacts -- no model, no generation. The mask is FROZEN per run into <SC_OUT>/mask_snapshot.py (workers re-import it each round; editing scripts/ mid-run is now safe). SC_MASK_REV=<commit>: run with the mask as of that commit -- the paired baseline arm of a mask A/B (e.g. 305105e = pre-typed mask). SC_DIFF=1: every spec-test pass is diff-judged vs gold (diff_c tuples); diff_kill = compile, not pass, and the item keeps sampling. Not comparable to plain-pass runs. Heavy: run it remotely.
